views.name: engagements_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  EngagementNumber,
  StartDate,
  EndDate,
  StartTime,
  StopTime,
  ContractPrice,
  CustomerID,
  AgentID,
  EntertainerID
FROM Engagements
views.description: Normalized one-row-per-engagement projection exposing engagement identifiers, temporal fields, price and foreign keys. Use this as the canonical Engagements row for analytics or further joins. | Use for: engagement counts over time; revenue/price aggregations per agent/customer/entertainer; temporal filtering (date ranges) or joining to calendars

views.name: agents_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AgentID,
  AgtFirstName,
  AgtLastName,
  AgtStreetAddress,
  AgtCity,
  AgtState,
  AgtZipCode,
  AgtPhoneNumber,
  DateHired,
  Salary,
  CommissionRate
FROM Agents
views.description: One-row-per-agent canonical projection exposing agent identity, contact info, hire date, salary and commission rate for joining into analytics. | Use for: agent headcount and tenure; commission or salary-based analyses; agent contact lists and joins to engagements

views.name: customers_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CustomerID,
  CustFirstName,
  CustLastName,
  CustStreetAddress,
  CustCity,
  CustState,
  CustZipCode,
  CustPhoneNumber
FROM Customers
views.description: One-row-per-customer projection exposing customer identity and contact/address attributes for joining to engagements and preference analysis. | Use for: customer engagement counts; geographic segmentation by CustCity/CustState; contact lists for outreach

views.name: entertainers_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  EntertainerID,
  EntStageName,
  EntSSN,
  EntStreetAddress,
  EntCity,
  EntState,
  EntZipCode,
  EntPhoneNumber,
  EntWebPage,
  EntEMailAddress,
  DateEntered
FROM Entertainers
views.description: One-row-per-entertainer projection with identity, contact and metadata. Useful for joining entertainer attributes to engagements and style/member bridges. | Use for: entertainer listing and contact; join entertainer attributes into engagement-level reports; filter entertainers by DateEntered

views.name: engagements_with_agents_customers_entertainers
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EngagementNumber,
  e.StartDate,
  e.EndDate,
  e.StartTime,
  e.StopTime,
  e.ContractPrice,
  e.CustomerID,
  c.CustFirstName,
  c.CustLastName,
  c.CustCity,
  c.CustState,
  e.AgentID,
  a.AgtFirstName,
  a.AgtLastName,
  a.AgtCity,
  a.AgtState,
  e.EntertainerID,
  en.EntStageName,
  en.EntCity,
  en.EntState
FROM Engagements e
LEFT JOIN Customers c ON e.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
LEFT JOIN Agents a ON e.AgentID = a.AgentID
LEFT JOIN Entertainers en ON e.EntertainerID = en.EntertainerID
views.description: Denormalized engagement-level relation joining Engagements to Agents, Customers and Entertainers to expose contact and descriptive attributes alongside contract price and dates. Use this for wide event-level reports. | Use for: report engagement revenue by agent/customer/entertainer attributes; list engagements with contact info for logistics; filter engagements by city/state of agent/customer/entertainer

views.name: entertainer_styles_wide
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  es.EntertainerID,
  es.StyleID,
  es.StyleStrength,
  ms.StyleName
FROM Entertainer_Styles es
LEFT JOIN Musical_Styles ms ON es.StyleID = ms.StyleID
views.description: One row per Entertainer-Style exposing style metadata and the bridge's StyleStrength. Useful for computing entertainer affinities, style-based filters, or joining to customer preferences. | Use for: find entertainers by musical style; aggregate style strengths per entertainer; join entertainer styles to customer preferences

views.name: customer_style_preferences
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mp.CustomerID,
  mp.StyleID,
  mp.PreferenceSeq,
  ms.StyleName
FROM Musical_Preferences mp
LEFT JOIN Musical_Styles ms ON mp.StyleID = ms.StyleID
views.description: One row per customer preferred style including preference sequence and style name; useful to compare customer tastes to entertainer styles or to filter engagements by preferred styles. | Use for: match customer preferences to entertainer offerings; segment customers by top preferences; recommend entertainers based on style overlap

views.name: engagements_monthly_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  strftime('%Y', StartDate) AS YearNumber,
  strftime('%m', StartDate) AS MonthNumber,
  COUNT(*) AS engagement_count,
  SUM(ContractPrice) AS total_contract_price
FROM Engagements
GROUP BY YearNumber, MonthNumber
views.description: Aggregated engagement-level measures rolled up by year and month (based on StartDate): counts and total ContractPrice. Use for monthly revenue and volume trends. Does not hardcode any specific year/month filters. | Use for: monthly revenue trends; volume of engagements over months; year-over-year month comparisons

views.name: agent_revenue_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AgentID,
  COUNT(*) AS engagement_count,
  SUM(ContractPrice) AS total_contract_price,
  AVG(ContractPrice) AS avg_contract_price
FROM Engagements
GROUP BY AgentID
views.description: Total engagements and total ContractPrice per AgentID. Useful for ranking agents by revenue, computing commission estimates, or joining to Agents for further attributes. | Use for: which agents generate most revenue; compute agent commissions (join to Agents.CommissionRate); agent workload by number of engagements

views.name: entertainer_member_list
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  em.EntertainerID,
  em.MemberID,
  em.Status,
  m.MbrFirstName,
  m.MbrLastName,
  m.MbrPhoneNumber,
  m.Gender
FROM Entertainer_Members em
LEFT JOIN Members m ON em.MemberID = m.MemberID
views.description: One row per Entertainer-Member association enriched with member name and contact. Useful to list members belonging to an entertainer or to count members per entertainer. | Use for: list members in a group; count active/inactive members per entertainer (if Status semantics known); contact members for lineup changes

views.name: calendar_days
views.description: Simple projection of calendar days from ztblDays for joining or filtering engagement dates. One row per DateField. | Use for: date scaffolding for time series; identify missing dates in engagement activity
